title: Wedding Slideshow Ideas: 20 Ways to Make It Worth Watching
description: 20 wedding slideshow ideas guests will watch: then-and-now pairs, parallel childhoods, voice notes, a guest-made brunch slideshow and where to play it.
dek: Story ideas, family and friends, the morning after, rehearsal games and what to skip.
excerpt: Twenty wedding slideshow ideas with why each works and how to do it, from then-and-now pairs to voice notes and a guest-made brunch slideshow, plus what to leave out.

faq.q: What should be included in a wedding slideshow?
faq.a: Photos of each of you growing up, how you met, your years together and the proposal, plus your families and friends. Most good slideshows end with photos of the guests in the room. Add short captions with places and years for older photos, a song change at each big chapter break, and a final slide that thanks everyone for coming. Leave out exes, inside jokes and anything that would embarrass someone else.

faq.q: When is the best time to show a wedding slideshow?
faq.a: For a single sit-down showing, right after the toasts works well, because guests are already seated and facing the front. If you’d rather not stop the night, run it as a loop during cocktail hour or dinner. Rehearsal dinners suit a longer, more playful version, and the morning-after brunch is a good place for a slideshow of the guests’ own photos.

faq.q: What’s the difference between a rehearsal dinner slideshow and a reception slideshow?
faq.a: The rehearsal dinner crowd is smaller and closer, so the slideshow can run longer, around 8 to 10 minutes, and include games, outtakes and inside stories. The reception slideshow plays to everyone, including guests who barely know you, so keep it to about 5 to 8 minutes, focused on your story and the people in the room.

faq.q: Can guests add their own photos to the slideshow?
faq.a: Yes. Before the wedding, ask for old photos through a shared album or upload link. For photos from the wedding itself, a shared camera app like Filmsera gathers everyone’s shots in one film, keeps them hidden until the reveal, then shows the whole roll and a short recap reel at once. That makes a slideshow of the guests’ photos easy to play at the brunch.

faq.q: How do you make a same-day wedding slideshow?
faq.a: Ask your photographer, since it depends on their workflow. Some offer it: they pick 50 to 100 images from the ceremony and portraits, edit them while guests eat dinner, then play the slideshow later in the reception, sometimes on a loop. You provide a screen or TV guests can see and a power outlet, and agree on the timing in advance so it fits around dinner and the toasts.

faq.q: Should you put exes in a wedding slideshow?
faq.a: No. Even a cropped photo can be recognized, and there is no upside for anyone in the room. If a great group photo includes an ex, pick a different one or leave that moment out. The same goes for photos from past relationships on trips or holidays: the slideshow is about the two of you and the people who are here now.
